title: Browser Use vs Browserbase vs Skyvern: compare the layer before the price
answer: These records describe overlapping browser-related offerings, but their units differ. Browser Use documents browser automation software and hosted offerings; Browserbase provides browser infrastructure and platform services; Skyvern describes browser workflow automation.
decision_questions: Do you need a browser runtime, a task-executing agent or both?
What is charged separately for models, traffic, proxies and retries?
What final state proves that your workflow succeeded?
conclusion: Editorial guidance: run the same allowed workflow on the relevant offering from each vendor. Compare cost per accepted completion, authentication behavior and interventions. No winner is established by this research.

title: MCP vs A2A vs Agent Client Protocol: different connection layers
answer: MCP connects applications to external capabilities and context. A2A concerns agent communication and task coordination. Agent Client Protocol connects coding agents with editors or IDEs. A system can use more than one of these layers.
decision_questions: Are you exposing a callable tool, coordinating with an agent or integrating an editor?
Which exact versions and authentication methods does each endpoint support?
Has the specific client/server pair been tested?
conclusion: Editorial guidance: choose the protocol for the interaction you need, then test the concrete implementation. The shared word agent does not make these protocols interchangeable.

title: x402, AP2, ERC-8004 and ERC-8183: payments, authority, identity and jobs
answer: These records cover different concerns. x402 describes HTTP resource payments; AP2 describes payment authorization mandates; ERC-8004 proposes identity, reputation and validation registries; ERC-8183 proposes job escrow with an evaluator.
decision_questions: Which party is authorized to spend?
What identifies the provider, and what supports its reputation?
Who evaluates delivery, and what causes settlement or release?
conclusion: Editorial guidance: model identity, authorization, payment and work acceptance separately. These sources do not establish a universal interoperable stack.
